minor.issue: Planning-vs-action classification gap: 'Choose a paint color for the bedroom' returns verdict=allow_with_warning (risk 2, PPE=[Ventilation, Gloves as needed]) instead of allow (risk 0-1, no PPE) as specified in the review request. Root cause: safety_engine.ppe_for() matches the substring 'paint' inside 'paint color', triggering the PPE_RULES paint entry; then evaluate_action step 4 (`if warns or ppe:`) unconditionally emits allow_with_warning. There is no distinction between planning intents (choose/pick/select/browse a paint color) and action intents (paint the wall). Reference: /app/backend/safety_engine.py:40-54, 155-159. Fix suggestion: (a) add a planning-verb guard at the top of evaluate_action that short-circuits to allow when the text starts with choose/pick/select/decide/browse and the noun is a material/color/style; or (b) tighten the paint PPE trigger to require verb forms (painting/paint the/prime/stain/apply) rather than the bare noun 'paint'; or (c) add negative-context phrases like 'paint color', 'color of paint', 'paint palette', 'paint sample', 'paint swatch' that suppress PPE.

action_items: Fix safety_engine.evaluate_action so 'Choose a paint color for the bedroom' returns verdict=allow / risk 0-1 / no PPE (see backend_issues.minor for suggested strategies). Once fixed, rerun test_safety_engine_doc43_iter93.py::TestVerdictMatrix::test_paint_color_choice_allow to confirm green.
critical_code_review_comments: safety_engine.ppe_for() uses raw substring keyword matching on lower-cased text without part-of-speech or verb/adjective context. 'paint' matches inside 'paint color' (planning) exactly the same as inside 'paint the wall' (action). The same pattern risk applies to other PPE_RULES entries: 'drill' matches 'drill bit set' or 'buy a drill', 'saw' matches 'I saw the crack' (though the false-positive rate is low for verbs used as past tense). Consider a small verb allowlist per rule.

evaluate_action step 4 escalates to allow_with_warning whenever `warns or ppe` is truthy — with no threshold. This means ANY task text mentioning a PPE-associated noun (paint sample, drill bit, ladder brand, tile pattern) triggers a warning verdict. Combined with the substring-matcher weakness above, this makes the planning→action boundary very leaky.

safety_engine.record_event silently swallows exceptions (bare except: pass at line 181-182). If Mongo insert fails during a real safety event, that failure is invisible. Consider logging at least a warning through the passed-in `_logger`.

record_event only calls admin_ops_engine.record_safety_escalation on escalate/block verdicts — good scope. But the trigger_type is `safety_engine_{source}` where source defaults to 'manual_check'; consumers scanning the ledger see safety_engine_manual_check, safety_engine_test_iter93, etc. — good disambiguation, worth documenting.

GET /api/hi/safety/events limits to 20 rows without a `limit` query param — fine for the personal panel but callers can't page further. Admin route accepts limit up to 200 which is consistent with the ledger's use case.
PPE catalog is deduped-and-sorted from PPE_RULES on every /meta call. With 18 items and low request rate this is fine, but the sorted-set expression could be cached at module load.

compose_action.ppe attachment (ar_guidance_engine.py:175-179) wraps the import in try/except so if safety_engine import ever fails, ppe silently becomes []; verified working — but consider warning-logging on import failure so silent regressions are visible.

rca_of_issue: BUG: POST /api/hi/safety/evaluate {text: 'Choose a paint color for the bedroom'} → verdict=allow_with_warning instead of allow. REPRODUCE: curl -X POST $BASE/api/hi/safety/evaluate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <demo>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"Choose a paint color for the bedroom"}'. ROOT CAUSE: /app/backend/safety_engine.py ppe_for() (line 107-115) does substring keyword matching on lower-cased text. Rule at line 44 `(['paint','primer','stain','sealant'], ['Ventilation','Gloves as needed'])` fires because 'paint color' contains 'paint'. evaluate_action step 4 (line 155-159) then triggers `if warns or ppe:` → return allow_with_warning. There's no planning-intent guard. MITIGATION: In evaluate_action, add a planning-context short-circuit before step 4: `planning_verbs = ('choose ', 'pick ', 'select ', 'decide ', 'browse ', 'compare '); planning_nouns = ('color', 'shade', 'sample', 'swatch', 'palette', 'style'); if any(v in t for v in planning_verbs) and any(n in t for n in planning_nouns): return {'verdict': 'allow', 'risk_level': 0, ...}`. Alternatively, tighten the paint rule keywords from bare 'paint' to action forms: ['painting', 'paint the', 'paint a', 'paint over', 'prime the', 'stain the', 'apply sealant'].
